bootstrap.interval: paired-user percentile descriptive 95%, all three cohorts

conditional_refit: one frozen winner only; no CSV if none qualifies
controls: reproduce exact Stage 12 lists and independently recompute saved metric values, not rounded inputs
data: unchanged two Stage 8 splits, labels, 1260 users, cohorts, pools and temporal boundaries
diagnostics: existing repeat50 relevant-pair and eligible-history <20/>=20 partitions, not model or selection variants

fixed.EASE_input: training-only globally scaled log1p >=80% qualifying-airing counts, exact Stage 12 scalar
fixed.S9: exact .70 normalized adjusted repeat50 + .30 normalized AR80; no additional S9 normalization

fallback_ranking.fallback: cutoff-specific >=80% training popularity restricted to the applicable candidate pool
fallback_ranking.fusion: weighted sum of normalized scores; no score rounding
fallback_ranking.normalization: per-user max normalization over eligible candidate scores

reuse: Stage 12 lambda1000 raw completed EASE score caches and verified S9 scores; no historical EASE refits needed

selection.cost_scope: direct EASE component adjustment/normalization and fusion/ranking plus reused measured EASE fit/query cost; shared component-attributed, not standalone end-to-end measurement
selection.objective: maximize minimum gain across two splits
selection.tie_break: lower measured computational cost summed across splits

uncertainty: overlapping and repeatedly used historical periods; selection-unadjusted intervals; no independent statistical confirmation

variant_E.counts: Stage 8 ownership, identity dedupe, labelled positive training airings fully before cutoff; target starts inside window including end crossings
variant_E.only_change: EASE opportunity adjustment; beta .10 and S9 unchanged
variant_E.order: complete weighted-EASE prediction, clip scores to zero, multiply eligible positive scores by factor, then per-user candidate-only max normalization
variant_E.positive_score_missing_historical_opport: raise inconsistency, do not invent a denominator
